newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clinton takes to Spain's holiday island.
newsitem.headline: Clinton takes to Spain's holiday island.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton wrapped up his brief vacation to the Spanish resort island of Majorca on Monday, joking that he wished he could delay the start of the NATO summit in Madrid to stay longer.

Clinton and his wife Hillary spent more than an hour strolling through the narrow streets of the city's old district with Spanish King Juan Carlos and Queen Sofia, stopping at one point to tour the former home of a 14th century nobleman.

"I'd like to stay," Clinton said to a reporter. "Wouldn't you like to stay, spend a few more days? We've been waiting 50 years to expand NATO, we can wait a few more days," he said grinning broadly. "I love it."
The summit, which begins officially on Tuesday morning, is widely expected to approve the admission to NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) of Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.

The Clinton family vacation in Majorca as guests of the king began on Saturday. The president and first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton planned to give the king and queen a tour of Air Force One before heading to Madrid.
Clinton was scheduled to meet Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in Madrid on Monday evening before attending a dinner for NATO leaders hosted by Aznar.
